decisions.summary: The inventory's discovery method, with each entry sorted into pattern 1 (asked before placing, kept), 2 (placed then repaired) or 3 (asked only of the finished map), plus its share of R1's failures.

Those points are: asked of a candidate before placing; nothing placed and then repaired; a finished-map check only as a backstop (by the GM's amendment, in the cohort and tests only); and where no candidate is admitted, more room. The three patterns have no slot for point 4. A placer that drops, relaxes or refuses where the remedy is room (last_resort.py dropping ordinary lanes or raising WebRefused, SiteRefused, OverlapRefused as a backstop at record time) is not labeled as a point-4 breach. A rule coded twice is found ('every pair of functions judging one rule') but fits none of the patterns, and neither does a finished-map check run mid-map. Nothing makes it necessary and nothing in the GM's words implies it. Fix: the patterns can stay as a grouping, but each entry must record which of the four points it breaks (or that it is coded twice). The discovery list must also name the sites where a placer that finds no admitted candidate drops, relaxes or refuses instead of being given room.

decisions.summary: The inventory reading is split by package (ways, homesteads/homestead_parts, waterfields, overlap registry, the rest), each package read by a sonnet Explore agent given 'D3's four questions'; the session checks each REPORTED entry against the code
decisions.why: FR-002 asks that EVERY repair pass, finished-map-only rule, rule coded more than once and in-generator check be listed. D3 makes that a method of enumerated searches: (1) every STEPS function and after-the-web pass; (2) every cohort_audit rule with its callers inside l7r/; (3) every caller of law.violations, lane_violators, row_rules, grove_rules and the overlap matrix inside the generator's run; (4) every pair of functions judging one rule; (5) every no-candidate drop/relax/refuse site. Entries are classed against the four points OR as 'its rule is coded twice'. D10 narrows this in two ways. (a) 'D3's four questions' does not match D3. There are four points plus a fifth class, coded-twice, and five searches. Whichever four are meant, one of D3's searches is not asked: coded-twice if the four are the points, the refusal sites if they are FR-002's four kinds. (b) Searches (2), (3) and (4) cross package lines. They follow a rule into cohort_audit, a check function to its callers inside the generator, and one rule to its second implementation. The likeliest duplicate, a rule in a placer package and again in the audit or check, lands in two different agents' reads, and neither sees the pair. The session checking each reported entry keeps a fetched claim out of R2 but finds nothing no agent reported, so completeness ('every', SC-007) is lost. A per-package split is not impossible to square with D3, so the narrowing is not forced. Fix: give each agent D3's full search list, coded-twice named. The session runs searches (2), (3) and (4) over the whole tree itself and reconciles their hits against R2 before T03 is done.

decisions.summary: T26 deletes only the post-lay stage_web passes measured NEEDLESS; a pass whose removal turns a fixed/pinned seed red (or moves a pool map's verdict) is recorded with its seeds and set down, untouched, for T06 / the GM's fixing pass.
decisions.why: FR-004 asks that every pass repairing a laid web be deleted; T26 deletes only part of them now. That is implied by the GM's own words of 2026-10-25 ('do all of that stuff, and then stop so we can slowly and deliberately go through the actual fixing where we get more seeds to pass'), as D11 carries them: a conversion that cannot land green without seed-by-seed work is recorded and set down, never iterated on. A pass whose deletion turns seeds red is exactly that fixing work. The purpose survives: no needed pass is kept by preference, each is recorded for T06, which rebuilds in the placers what it stands in for (FR-004/FR-006), or for the GM.

decisions.summary: One probe per pass, run in a detached worktree at landed HEAD; that pass's call sites are switched off by an environment switch that never lands; each probe rolls make cohort N=48 FRESH=0 against an all-passes-on baseline.
decisions.why: This is how the measurement is taken, and the instrument never lands. It settles nothing the request or spec leaves open about what is built. The 'one probe, no tuning' rule (item 7) applies D11's 'never iterated on'.

decisions.summary: A pass is NEEDLESS when every fixed and pinned seed keeps its baseline verdict with the pass off; maps may differ.
decisions.why: The test is FR-008's landing condition, so it decides only WHEN a deletion FR-004 already asks for can land under D11, not WHETHER it is owed. A looser bar deletes more repair passes, which moves toward the request. Aside, not a fidelity finding: the probe as D22 states it does not roll the pool maps, though exit 6 counts a pool-map verdict change as NEEDED. Under D23 the landing's FR-008 run would still catch such a pass, so nothing slips through.

decisions.summary: The needless passes, their call sites and the tests that only exercised them are deleted together in one landing; if that landing is red the whole deletion is set down and recorded, with no pass-by-pass iteration.
decisions.why: In that one contingency it leaves undeleted passes FR-004 asks to delete, and it does not bisect the set. D11 (the GM's stop line, already ruled in MODE 1) says such a conversion is 'recorded and set down, never iterated on'. The GM asked that the fixing be done 'slowly and deliberately' with them, not overnight. Untangling which joint deletions interact is that fixing, so stopping is what the GM asked for, not a departure from it. Deleting the tests that only exercised deleted code goes with FR-004's deletion and SC-004's smaller engine.

decisions.summary: Maps may change as a result of the deletions, held to the claims and the cohort.
decisions.why: FR-004 deletes passes that change laid webs, so maps moving is the requested effect. FR-008 (cohort, pinned rows, pool maps, research claims) is the bar held, as the spec says.

decisions.summary: T26 runs after T23/T25 and before T06.
decisions.why: This is ordering inside the feature. D11 puts the tasks that move no map first, and T26 moves maps, so it comes after them. T06 is a FR-004 conversion that D11 keeps in scope.
